correctness.rationale: For odd squarefree n>1, the Möbius polynomial is integral over Z_2. On even x=2s, M_n(2s)/2 has linear coefficient mu(n)/n odd and nonlinear terms divisible by 4; it is a bijective isometry. For odd x=epsilon+4s, H(z)=M_n(sqrt(z))/sqrt(z) has H(1)=0 and expansion H(1+8t)=2^e(ut+2Q(t)) with e=2+nu2(phi(n)), u odd: the positive-power Mobius divisor sums factor as product (p^r-1), divisible by phi(n); higher Taylor terms have valuation at least e+1. Both normalized odd-class branches are isometries, so every even output gets one even preimage and 2^{min(k,e)-1} extra odd preimages exactly when divisible by 2^{min(k,e)}. For odd nonsquarefree n, smallest nonvanishing exponent multiple n/rad(n)>=3 and odd x powers congruent x modulo 8, forcing image inside 8Z_2. Checked n=3,5,15,21,35 and k=1,2,3,5,7 independently by complete modular histogram (25 cases); this does not prove infinite quantifiers.
